tool_args.rationale: The branch-discriminating measurements extend sink gradient from about 1 to 0.18 and 2.35; at comparable inputs, output is higher at low sink and lower at high sink, while the input response remains monotone and concave. This matches the archived node-C static siphon with a positive square-root branch. Fit its parameters numerically and use the fresh confirmation to test adequacy.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Already acquired; its low/high sink-gradient rows resolve the square-root branch as positive.
All available observations share H=0.6 and the archived ODE requires at least eight trajectory rows; the observed concave input response and sink sensitivity support the simpler static siphon law.

It could also yield concavity, but the pilot signatures and archived node-C mechanism directly describe the observed base-field plus sink-inhibition and open-branch pattern; defer the extra complexity.
Irrelevant to distinguishing the plausible target mechanisms and explicitly not worth its cost.
